newsitem.title: USA: Lyondell earnings aided by refinery upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Lyondell earnings aided by refinery upgrade.

text.p: Lyondell Petrochemical Co said Monday that a refining upgrade at its 265,000 barrel per day (bpd) Lyondell-Citgo Refining Co (LCR) joint venture would stabilize and improve earnings and cash flow.

"Strong operating performance, combined with higher volumes of heavy Venezuelan crude oil processed under the crude supply agreement, enabled LCR to contribute $6 million to Lyondell's results for the quarter, versus a loss of $23 million in the fourth quarter of last year," the company said in a statement with earnings.
Lyondell has a 60 percent of the venture with Venezuelan owned Citgo.

The upgrade was in service as of March 1, one month ahead of schedule. The $1.1 billion project upgraded the refinery's capacity to process over 215,000 bpd of heavy crude oil when in full conversion mode.

"We began to see the benefits of this accomplishment in first quarter results and believe that LCR is on track toward a significant improvement in earnings and cash flow as the new units are optimized," said Dan Smith, Lyondell's chief executive.
Operating at Lyondell's petrochemicals division was $83 million in the first quarter, versus $57 million in the fourth quarter of 1996, excluding one time items from a year ago.
"Profitability improved significantly over the year ago first quarter primarily due to higher product revenues," Smith said.

Operating earnings in polymers fell to $16 million in the from to $28 million in the fourth quarter of 1996, primarily due to lower product prices, higher feedstock costs, and lower sales volumes due to a planned maintenance turnaround at the company's Matagorda plant.
Smith said polymer margins began to improve late in the quarter as a result of price increases for high density and low density polyethylene implemented.
"We are seeing continuing strong sales demand for petrochemicals and polymers as we enter the second quarter and feedstock costs appear to be stabilizing," he added.
